Inbound signup from YC demo day ad; founder-led engineering team building an embedded chat widget for mid-market SaaS apps. Trial started 2026-02-25. Discovery call 2026-03-02 (Sophie + CTO Maya Chen). Key points:
- Primary workload: low-latency streaming chat inside product UI (token-by-token updates). Several micro-interactions per session.
- Target latency (perceived): user expects typing/streaming updates to start <250ms and steady per-token latency <100-200ms; p99 target for message surface = <400ms.
- Scale: pilot ~50 daily active users, goal to 5000 DAU in 12 months; concurrent chat connections in pilot ~10-25, peak expected 100+.
- Cost sensitivity: early-stage, careful about per-token spend; prefer hosted API with predictable unit pricing and burst limits.
- Model preference: open/efficient models acceptable (4B-13B), quantized variants fine; want streaming and function/tool calling later.
- Reliability: fallback to smaller/cheaper model when capacity constrained. Must avoid visible latency spikes.
- Security: SSO (SAML) for admin console, audit logs for API access, data retention policy controls. No on-prem requirement for now.
- Integration: single-page app (React) will use streaming SDK/HTTP SSE/Websocket; wants examples and snippet for prefix caching and token streaming.
- Eval criteria: end-to-end perceived latency (UX), token cost per session, error rate on tool calls, model quality for short conversational replies.
- Quote from CTO: "If responses feel slow users drop out — we need the stream to feel instant."
